title: Your GPU Neighbor Can Hear Your Model — Branislav Brzak, Stealthium
talk_summary: A GPU side-channel research talk showing that co-tenants on shared H100 hardware (MIG partitions or NVLink-connected GPUs) can infer a model's identity, decode speed, layer count, and workload type purely from timing measurements, without touching victim data. The only actionable content is defensive: placement of untrusted tenants, awareness of MIG vs NVLink leakage tradeoffs, and kernel-level monitoring.

takeaways.technique: Tenant placement / isolation awareness for shared GPU hosts
takeaways.what_they_do: They show that MIG partitions isolate compute and VRAM but not GPU-wide memory barriers, so timing leaks persist; they recommend not co-locating untrusted tenants with sensitive models and understanding MIG vs NVLink leakage tradeoffs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: no coloquen los segmentos MIG de un inquilino no confiable junto a un modelo sensible
takeaways.numbers: 97% model identification, 99.3% decode-speed accuracy, 79.2% over NVLink

takeaways.technique: Kernel-level workload monitoring for anomalous probing
takeaways.what_they_do: Their product detects side-channel attacks by watching kernel launches: a kernel relaunched ~3,000 times over the same 40KB buffer with almost no data returned to CPU is flagged as a timing probe.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Un solo kernel se relanzó unas 3,000 veces accediendo exactamente a los mismos 40 kilobytes de memoria
takeaways.numbers: ~3,000 relaunches, 40KB buffer, 1KB returned to CPU, detected in <600ms
